text:
Asha R: heads-up — nightly regression on weight-only INT8 after landing the AWQ group-size remap. p50 latency up ~12% on small-chat workload. perf-bot shows a spike in pack/unpack time. anyone seen this before? :thinking:

Jorge L: saw the alert. first guess: remap changed group boundaries which increased partial-group writes during packing. can you paste the perf-bot snippet?

Asha R: here are the two salient lines from last night: 

```
perf-bot: run=nightly-int8-aws-8x1, model=gpt-small, tokens=512
pack_stats: avg_pack_us=112.3, unpack_us=18.7, pack_tail_pct=24.1
kernel_select: awq_group=8 -> kernel=awq-opt-v2
kvcache_hit_rate=0.91, kv_copy_us=6.2
```

Maya K: 112us avg pack is high for that infra. our baseline for group=8 was ~95us. Was the kernel switched to the serial pack path? that often increases tail.

Alex P: I instrumented the pack hotpath yesterday — the remap created more misaligned 4-byte block tail writes which forced the fallback memmove in pack_unaligned(). rough patch: when group-size % 4 != 0 we fall into slow path.

Ciara S: @Alex can you share the trace? also which quant backend — AWQ or GPTQ? we tuned AWQ remap but nightly uses combo-variants.

Alex P: trace attached (summarized):
- time in pack_loop: 68us
- pack_unaligned/memmove: 30us (was 8us before)
- kernel_dispatch wait: 9us (unchanged)

Asha R: so pack_unaligned exploded. linking that to AWQ remap change seems plausible. Jorge — do kernel chooser heuristics treat remapped groups differently?

Jorge L: chooser picks kernel based on (group_size, bytes_per_group, model_arch). remap mutated bytes_per_group distribution: some groups went up from 16 -> 20 bytes which crosses our 16-byte fast-path boundary. chooser then routes to awq-opt-v2 which expects aligned contiguous blocks; when not aligned we still call it but we do prepack into an aligned staging buffer, causing extra memcpys.

Maya K: two prongs: adjust remap to keep bytes_per_group <=16 where possible, or improve pack to avoid memcopies (SIMD-friendly rewriter). quick win is to add a chooser fallback to prefer kernel with in-place tolerant path when pack tail ratio > X.

Asha R: agree. short-term: patch chooser to prefer awq-compat kernel for groups that produce nonzero tail_pct. long-term: reduce packing overhead by adding vectorized tail-handling.

Ciara S: also seeing KV cache interaction: when pack overhead increases, per-request worker stalls while kv_copy waits, increasing end-to-end p50. maybe add async kv copy so pack can stream?

Alex P: async KV copy buys concurrency but complicates KV lifetime. could try micro-batching change: if group packing time > threshold, allow overlapping pack and kv copy for next request in batch. that reduces p50 but may increase jitter.

perf-bot: note — regression correlated with commit 7f3a2b8 (awq_group_remap.patch). commit links: https://git/repo/commit/7f3a2b8 :warning:

Jorge L: plan proposal:
1) revert remap to previous mapping for nightly (hotfix) — target tonight.
2) prod patch: chooser fallback when tail_pct > 10% to prefer awq-compat kernel (low risk).
3) medium term: implement vectorized tail pack and add microbenchmark for partial-group occupancy.
4) explore async kv copy + overlap for high-latency pack paths (spike testing only).

Maya K: I'm +1 for (2) and (3). I'll open a PR for chooser fallback and add a microbenchmark harness in eng-ml/perf/pack_tail_bench.

Asha R: I'll revert remap in nightly and rerun. Alex — can you make a small repro script that toggles group->bytes mapping so we can run sweep? something like:

```
# repro driver
python tools/pack_repro.py --model gpt-small --group-map configs/group_map_v1.json --tokens 512 --runs 50
```

Alex P: on it, will push by EOD. includes perf counters for pack_unaligned hits.

Ciara S: also let's add a perf regression alert rule for pack_tail_pct > 15% to catch this earlier. I can add that to the console.

Asha R: thanks team. low-risk hotfix tonight, then chooser fallback PR tomorrow. keeping notes here for the postmortem. :thumbsup:

Jorge L: one more data point — GPTQ variants didn't regress as much because their remap kept bytes_per_group aligned to 16. so the interaction is very remap-backend-specific. important for rollout strategy.

Maya K: good call. we'll add a matrix of (backend x remap) in the pack_tail_bench so future remaps run across both AWQ and GPTQ kernels.

perf-bot: run queued: nightly-int8-aws-8x1 (post-revert) — will report in ~45m.
